name: It's Still Rock and Roll to Me

podcast.body: Billy Joel scored his first Hot 100 number one hit with this song in 1980. It served as a satirical diss against rock critics and the music press who favored "cutting-edge new wave" over his "unpretentious pop songs." Joel adopted the persona of a "hipster scribe infatuated with new wave" for the track. This song also notably became the inspiration for two more diss records in the 1980s. "Joel scored his first Hot 100 number one with a satirical diss of rock critics and the music press, who preferred cutting-edge new wave to his unpretentious pop songs."

podcast.body: This song was the winner of the 1980 Billboard Song of the Summer. It is described as a "clever riff on rockability and new wave trend hopping," and continues to be played on the radio. "It's still rock and roll to me 1980s Song of the Summer was a clever riff on rockability and new wave trend hopping, and it's still on the radio."
